standard_prerequisites.name: Every perfect complex is pseudo-coherent and the tensor product of two pseudo-coherent complexes is pseudo-coherent
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the implication from the first condition to the second and the trivial implication from the second to the third.

standard_prerequisites.name: The direct image of a pseudo-coherent complex along a flat proper morphism of finite presentation is pseudo-coherent
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the second condition from the first.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived category of quasi-coherent modules on projective space is equivalent to the derived category of modules over the graded algebra of the projective space, with the generator corresponding to the structure sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the problem be translated into a statement about modules over a ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived Hom over the ambient algebra computes the graded pieces of the tensor product with the generator, and pseudo-coherence descends along the equivalence
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the given complex is pseudo-coherent from the condition on the twists.

core_obligations: Record that the derived Hom from a perfect complex is computed as the derived global sections of the derived sheaf Hom, so conditions (3) and (4) are equivalent (proof lines 8794-8799).

Note that the second condition implies the third because every perfect complex is pseudo-coherent, and deduce the fifth condition from the third by taking the twists of the structure sheaf for the degrees zero to n (proof lines 8797-8808).

Show that the first condition implies the second: the tensor product of pseudo-coherent complexes is pseudo-coherent, and the direct image of a pseudo-coherent complex along the given morphism is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 8801-8806).

For the remaining direction, use the description of the projective space in terms of a graded algebra: the generator and the algebra are those appearing in the displayed equations, and the category of quasi-coherent modules on projective space is equivalent to the derived category of modules over that algebra via the tensor product with the generator (proof lines 8809-8820).

Translate the fifth condition into a statement about the derived Hom from the algebra to the module corresponding to the complex, use the identification of the derived Hom with the description of the complex and the condition on the twists to see that this derived Hom is pseudo-coherent, and apply the descent statement for pseudo-coherence over the algebra to conclude that the module, hence the original complex, is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 8821-8862).
proof_roadmap: The easy implications among the five conditions (proof lines 8794-8808).
Translate to modules over the projective space algebra via the generator (proof lines 8809-8820).
Use the derived Hom description and descend pseudo-coherence to reach the first condition (proof lines 8821-8862).
